{"status":"ready","summary":"Perfect hash joins whose build keys are sparse can now push an exact bloom filter into the probe scan. Sparse here means count*4 <= range+1. The filter is filled from the perfect hash table's own key bitmap, so building it costs almost nothing.

Changes:
1) In FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp), a perfect hashtable no longer rejects the BF outright. It is allowed through CanUseBloomFilter when the key range computed from the build min/max shows the keys are sparse. For perfect HTs only an exact BF is accepted: TrySetExactBloomFilter must succeed, otherwise nothing is deferred. SetBuildBloomFilter is not set, because the HT finalize never runs for a perfect HJ. This covers both the plain path and the compressed-materialization offset path.
2) New PerfectHashJoinExecutor::FillExactBloomFilter. It initializes the exact BF and inserts (build_min widened to 64 bits + slot) for every set bit of bitmap_build_idx, or every slot if the build is dense. It uses InsertExact, so a mismatch between the BF's min/range and the HT's could only set the overflow flag, which makes the filter pass everything. That is still correct. Types other than signed/unsigned integers up to 64 bits return false.
3) A new helper, PushPerfectHashJoinBloomFilters, fills the BF and pushes the deferred filters, then clears the list. It runs right after FinalizeFilters when use_perfect_hash is true, in both the serial Finalize path and the parallel PerfectHashJoinBuildEvent::FinishEvent (after FinishBuild). FinalizeFilters is already called with the final use_perfect_hash value, so when duplicates force the fallback to a regular HJ the old behaviour is unchanged. Nothing is pushed twice and no half-filled BF is pushed.

Verified: the lineitem scan now shows `l_suppkey IN BF(s_suppkey)`. On a supplier/nation micro query the scan output drops from 60M rows to 4.8M.

Bench (quick, 2 bindings x 4 hot runs; the tool says differences under ~5% are noise):
- q07: -11.5%, -12.9%, -17.7% across three runs
- q02: -19.7%, -21.8%, -7.3%
- Full suite geomean: -3.2%
- One-off outliers in the full run: q08 +10% and q19 +11% did not reproduce; reruns gave q08 -3.9% and +0.7%, q19 -1.5%. In the plans I looked at, the build sides those queries' scans would get a BF from have ranges over 1M, so the change should not apply to them.
- q13 (dense RIGHT perfect join) stayed in noise: +2.4% and +0.6%.

Correctness checks (all matched the expected counts):
- a join on keys shifted by -50000 (negative keys) vs the unshifted join
- a RIGHT join with an extra NULL build row
- a USMALLINT build key
- IS NOT DISTINCT FROM (no BF)

structured_output.summary:
Perfect hash joins whose build keys are sparse can now push an exact bloom filter into the probe scan. Sparse here means count*4 <= range+1. The filter is filled from the perfect hash table's own key bitmap, so building it costs almost nothing.

Changes:
1) In FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp), a perfect hashtable no longer rejects the BF outright. It is allowed through CanUseBloomFilter when the key range computed from the build min/max shows the keys are sparse. For perfect HTs only an exact BF is accepted: TrySetExactBloomFilter must succeed, otherwise nothing is deferred. SetBuildBloomFilter is not set, because the HT finalize never runs for a perfect HJ. This covers both the plain path and the compressed-materialization offset path.
2) New PerfectHashJoinExecutor::FillExactBloomFilter. It initializes the exact BF and inserts (build_min widened to 64 bits + slot) for every set bit of bitmap_build_idx, or every slot if the build is dense. It uses InsertExact, so a mismatch between the BF's min/range and the HT's could only set the overflow flag, which makes the filter pass everything. That is still correct. Types other than signed/unsigned integers up to 64 bits return false.
3) A new helper, PushPerfectHashJoinBloomFilters, fills the BF and pushes the deferred filters, then clears the list. It runs right after FinalizeFilters when use_perfect_hash is true, in both the serial Finalize path and the parallel PerfectHashJoinBuildEvent::FinishEvent (after FinishBuild). FinalizeFilters is already called with the final use_perfect_hash value, so when duplicates force the fallback to a regular HJ the old behaviour is unchanged. Nothing is pushed twice and no half-filled BF is pushed.

Verified: the lineitem scan now shows `l_suppkey IN BF(s_suppkey)`. On a supplier/nation micro query the scan output drops from 60M rows to 4.8M.

Bench (quick, 2 bindings x 4 hot runs; the tool says differences under ~5% are noise):
- q07: -11.5%, -12.9%, -17.7% across three runs
- q02: -19.7%, -21.8%, -7.3%
- Full suite geomean: -3.2%
- One-off outliers in the full run: q08 +10% and q19 +11% did not reproduce; reruns gave q08 -3.9% and +0.7%, q19 -1.5%. In the plans I looked at, the build sides those queries' scans would get a BF from have ranges over 1M, so the change should not apply to them.
- q13 (dense RIGHT perfect join) stayed in noise: +2.4% and +0.6%.

Correctness checks (all matched the expected counts):
- a join on keys shifted by -50000 (negative keys) vs the unshifted join
- a RIGHT join with an extra NULL build row
- a USMALLINT build key
- IS NOT DISTINCT FROM (no BF)
- a parallel-path build (199k sparse keys in a 1M range, customer→orders), checked against an aggregate-then-join plan
structured_output.generality:
This helps any single-key integer equi-join that takes the perfect-HJ path (range up to 1M) when the build side is a selective subset of a dimension (a region, nation or category filter) and it probes a large fact-table scan. With E0027's per-value select, the probe scan then skips decoding the non-key columns for rows that cannot match.

It does not apply in these cases:
- Dense builds (keys fill more than 25% of the range). They keep relying on min/max.
- Build ranges over 1M. Those use the regular HJ, which already gets a BF.
- Joins that treat NULLs as equal (IS NOT DISTINCT FROM).
- Keys wider than 64 bits.
- Probe columns behind a cast.

The normal guards still apply: build_side_has_filter, probe larger than build, and SelectivityOptionalFilter switches the filter off at runtime if it turns out unselective.
structured_output.notes:
I avoided changing bloom_filter.hpp. Filling the BF with InsertExact per set slot costs O(range/64 + keys), which is trivial below 1M. It also stays correct even if the HT's min differed from the BF's exact_min.

The q07 profile output gets truncated by the tool, so I checked the BF on the lineitem scan with a smaller three-table query run through `sql`.

Bench noise is about ±10% on q08/q19, so rerun outliers before trusting them.

Follow-up idea: q08 and q19 build sides (part, customer) have ranges between 1.5M and 2M, which is over the perfect-HJ limit, so they use the regular-HT exact BF path instead.
